uncited: Reparameterization estimators compute gradients of rendering integrals by transforming the integration domain or sampling distribution such that the dependence on scene parameters $\theta$ is moved from the domain boundaries or probability density functions (PDFs) into the integrand's argument.
The core mechanism is the application of the change of variables formula to the rendering integral $I(\theta) = \int_{\Omega_\theta} f(x, \theta) dx$.
In Monte Carlo estimation, this is implemented by sampling points $\omega$ from a fixed distribution $p(\omega)$ on $\Omega$, mapping them to $x = T(\omega, \theta)$, and weighting by the Jacobian.
- **Formula**: The combined estimator is derived by plugging the Monte Carlo-based estimator (Equation 5) into the volume rendering estimator (Equation 3).

In computer graphics, the application to rendering was driven by the need to handle visibility discontinuities (silhouettes and shadows) which cause non-differentiable jumps in the rendering integral when scene parameters change.

The specific formulation for volume rendering and path tracing involves mapping parameter-dependent domains (such as the set of visible points or the sampling distribution induced by density) to fixed reference domains.
